description: R6 claims `detail` for the brain_transport (wake_error) case is `err.message`, and that this string is 'ALREADY-redacted' / that R6 'adds no new redaction pass' because it reuses a value 'already passed through redactPrivateKeyPatterns upstream'. This is factually false for the wake_error/brain_transport branch specifically. Read runtime/loop/index.mjs:351-364 (the THINK catch block) fresh: `err.message` is used only in a `process.stderr.write` call and in a hardcoded-string ledger field (`error: 'proxy_down'`, NOT the real err.message) -- it is never passed to `redactPrivateKeyPatterns` anywhere in this catch block or upstream. Traced upstream into runtime/loop/brain.mjs (the `think()` function this err comes from): `thinkProxy`'s httpPost rejects with `new Error(\`HTTP ${res.statusCode}: ${data.slice(0,300)}\`)` (raw upstream response body, brain.mjs:179) and `new Error(\`proxy_down: ${lastErr?.message}\`)` (brain.mjs:78); `thinkClaudeP` rejects with `new Error(\`claude_exit_${code}: ${stderr.slice(0,200)}\`)` (raw, unfiltered child-process stderr, brain.mjs:130) and similar raw-stderr/stdout-derived messages elsewhere in the same function. None of these error-construction sites call `redactPrivateKeyPatterns` or `scrubPrivateKeys` on the resulting message text (scrubPrivateKeys is only applied to the child ENV passed into the claude-p subprocess, a completely different data flow -- REQ-004's private-key-isolation guarantee covers the env, not the subprocess's own stderr/stdout content). The codebase's existing engineering discipline treats exactly this class of value (subprocess/HTTP output) as requiring explicit redaction before persistence -- confirmed by index.mjs applying redactPrivateKeyPatterns to skillResult.output TWICE (once inside runSkillWithKillRef via `redact(output)`, once again at ledger-write time). R6, as literally worded, would make err.message the FIRST unredacted secret-bearing value ever persisted to disk in this codebase's history, writing up to 4000 raw characters of upstream HTTP response body / subprocess stderr verbatim into a new file (harness-failures.jsonl) under the false premise that no new redaction pass is needed. If a proxy error body or claude-p stderr ever echoes a credential (plausible: e.g. an Authorization header reflected in an error page, or a crashed subprocess dumping an env-derived string it read directly rather than via the scrubbed childEnv), it would leak into this new persistent file unredacted -- a genuine regression against REQ-004/PROP-020 that R9 ('backward compatibility / non-interference') claims this feature fully preserves. Fix: R6 must apply `redactPrivateKeyPatterns(err.message)` explicitly for the brain_transport branch (this is a NEW redaction call site this feature must add, not a reuse of an existing one).

evidence.snippet: R6 ... `detail` is the ALREADY-redacted string in scope at that point (`err.message` for `brain_transport`; `skillResult.output` for the others -- both already passed through `redactPrivateKeyPatterns` upstream, R6 adds no new redaction pass). Contradicted by runtime/loop/index.mjs:351-364 (err.message never redacted) and runtime/loop/brain.mjs:78,130,179 (raw HTTP-body / subprocess-stderr strings embedded directly into thrown Error messages, no redaction call anywhere on that path).
